title: UX-driven PRD: Hosted LLM surface (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank) — acceptance matrix & staged launch scenarios
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary:
This PRD defines a UX-driven hosted inference surface that harmonizes chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank endpoints into a consistent, opinionated developer experience focused on predictability and cost-awareness. The goal is a minimal, discoverable API bundle plus companion acceptance gates and runbook for a staged launch.

Background & motivation:
- Customers repeatedly ask for a single predictable surface to support common LLM patterns (chat-style multi-turn, single-shot completions, searching/embeddings, and rerank flows).
- Inconsistent parameter names, streaming behavior, and output shapes across endpoints cause integration friction and regressions in downstream apps.
- Engineering priorities: reduce onboarding time, prevent common integration errors, and enable telemetry to tie UX choices to unit economics.

Goals (measurable):
1) Reduce integration issues reported by early partners by 60% in first 90 days.
2) Deliver a single canonical SDK surface + REST contract covering chat/completions/embeddings/rerank.
3) Streaming parity for chat/completions with function-calling compatibility.
4) Acceptance gates: latency P50 < 80ms for embeddings-128 tokens and < 150ms for chat generation (short prompts) on hosted tier.
5) Launch with automated evals that validate quality delta <= 2% vs baseline model for representative prompts.

Scope (what's in):
- API contract with unified naming (messages vs prompt, model, temperature, max_tokens, response_format).
- Streaming support and structured output (JSON schema / canonical tool-calling envelope).
- Embeddings endpoint standardized to return similarity-normalized vectors and deterministic hashing header.
- Rerank pipeline defined as a light-weight REST adapter that accepts batched candidate vectors and returns ranked ids with scores.
- Console pages for per-endpoint latency/cost and a launch checklist entry.

Out of scope (for this ticket):
- Deep multi-modal payloads (image/video).
- Dedicated capacity autoscaling changes.
- Enterprise VPC-only deployment packaging (handled by Private team).

Acceptance criteria (gated, must all pass):
acceptance_criteria: API: single canonical OpenAPI spec published; example clients (python/js) that call chat/completions/embeddings/rerank with identical auth and model selection parameters.
Behavioral: streaming frames begin within 150ms for 90% of chat requests in canary region under baseline load (see metrics).
Compatibility: function/tool-calling envelope accepted by both chat and completions SDK helpers with the same validation behavior.
Embeddings: vectors must be deterministic for identical inputs with seed header; average L2 variance across 10k identical inputs = 0.
Rerank: latency for a 10-candidate batch < 200ms 95th percentile in canary; ranking stable across retries (rank idempotency test).
Quality: eval suite (1000 prompt pairs per surface) must show generation and rerank regression <= 2% w.r.t. baseline models on curated metrics.
Telemetry: per-route token/latency/cost breakdown recorded and visible in Console for the canary orgs; retention for 30d for launch window.
Docs: Quickstart, migration guide, and determinism notes published in Confluence and docs.redwood.ai with runnable examples.
Operational: runbook created with rollback instructions and gradation thresholds for canary, partial, and full rollout.
Security & compliance: security review completed and flag 'security_review_required' resolved; no P0 security findings outstanding.
launch_checklist: Publish OpenAPI + SDK samples to npm/pypi and point docs to latest spec URL.
Canary rollout to 3 low-risk tenants with telemetry hooks wired (latency/cost/quality).
Execute eval harness (generation + rerank + embedding stability) and upload report to Confluence.
Create Console landing page with per-route cost breakdown and an alert rule for cost anomalies.
Ops runbook verified by on-call guild; runbook linked in Console and incident runbooks.
GitHub PRs for runtime changes merged and tagged with release note draft.
Security review sign-off and KMS integration smoke test completed.
Prepare migration notes for customers: common parameter mappings and breaking changes.
Define and schedule staged traffic ramp (canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%) with automated rollback thresholds.
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (Canary, 7 days): 3 partner tenants, monitor latency/cost/quality. Stage 2 (Slice, 3 days): 10% of self-serve traffic routed, automated watch for regressions. Stage 3 (Expansion, 2 days): 50% traffic, increase sampling of evals. Stage 4 (Full): full route switch; post-launch 30-day monitoring with weekly quality checks. Rollback triggers include sustained quality regression > 3%, latency SRE SLO breach > 5%, or cost anomalies > 20% vs baseline.
metrics: integration error rate (4xx/5xx) for first 90 days
open_questions: Do we coerce the rerank input schema to strictly require embeddings or allow raw text (and run embeddings server-side)?
What is the default deterministic-seed header value and should it be opt-out or opt-in for embeddings?
Are we offering separate QoS lanes (fast/cheap) at launch or deferring to a later iteration?
decisions: Use 'messages' nomenclature across chat and completions to simplify SDK helpers (decision date: 2026-03-05, owner: Ravi Kapoor).

Embedding vectors are deterministic by default when 'x-rw-deterministic: true' header is present; default omitted to preserve previously observed non-determinism for legacy customers (decision date: 2026-03-09).
risks: Quality regressions for generation when model variants are swapped for cost reasons; mitigation: eval gating and canary sampling.
Customers integrating older SDKs may experience parameter mismatches; mitigation: migration shim in SDKs and server-side mapping for 30 days.
Telemetry volume increase causing storage/cost spike; mitigation:  sampling strategy and 30d retention cap for launch window.
